items.prompt: A good commit subject is usually…
choices: A long paste of the entire diff
Short, imperative, and focused on the change
Always empty so Git invents one
items.explain: Prefer a short imperative subject (e.g. Add mul path to ALU), not a dump of the patch.

items.prompt: The commit body is best used to…
choices: Repeat the subject in all caps
Explain why the change happened and how to verify it
List every untracked file in the home directory
items.explain: Body carries context: motivation and how a reviewer can check the result.

items.prompt: "fixed stuff" is a strong commit message for coursework delivery.
items.explain: Vague messages hide intent; future you and reviewers need a clear subject (and often a why).

items.prompt: git log --oneline is useful because it shows…
choices: A short hash plus each commit subject
items.explain: One-line log is a quick timeline of subjects—another reason to write them well.
